dedupe_keys.name: england projected population health and healthcare resource requirements 2025 to 2047

description: This case study projects how population health, demographics and the healthcare resources they require could change over two decades for an integrated care system in England. The authors, researchers working with the Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire health system, modelled a population of about one million residents moving between health states from 2025 to 2047 and attached healthcare use and costs to each state, and posted the work as a preprint, free to read online on medRxiv under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial licence. Coverage is one integrated care system in the south west of England. Caveats: the preprint has not been peer reviewed, the linked patient data are not public, and results depend on assumed transition rates and costs. The study found that healthcare costs would grow by 15 to 22 percent while the population grows by 4 to 16 percent, so cost per person rises by 5 to 11 percent; keeping costs in line with population would need a 4 percent productivity gain or a 10 percent reduction in transitions to worse health states. Simulation uses: long-run demand scenarios for health system capacity planning and investment appraisal. Related records: the ESRI Ireland hospital demand projections (data-esri-ireland-public-acute-hospital-demand-projections-2040) give a comparable national exercise.
